payload.report: The 10-year-old rural patient has intermittent abdominal pain, anal itching, and nighttime restlessness for 2-3 weeks. Stool O&P twice revealed 70 µm spherical yellow thick-shelled eggs with six hooklets and no polar filaments. The laboratory physician confirmed this morphology is diagnostic for Hymenolepis diminuta and excludes Enterobius vermicularis. This directly confirms a parasitic intestinal infection, specifically H. diminuta. Normal physical exam, blood/urine tests, and absent eosinophilia do not contradict the diagnosis. Therefore, the diagnosis is Hymenolepis diminuta infection.
